questions.question: What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 2-meter band?

choices.A: Plus or minus 5 MHz
choices.B: Plus or minus 600 kHz
choices.C: Plus or minus 500 kHz
choices.D: Plus or minus 1 MHz

questions.answer: Plus or minus 600 kHz

questions.question: What is the national calling frequency for FM simplex operations in the 2-meter band?
What is a common repeater frequency offset in the 70-centimeter band?

choices.A: Plus or minus 5 MHz
choices.B: Plus or minus 600 kHz
choices.C: Plus or minus 500 kHz
choices.D: Plus or minus 1 MHz

questions.answer: Plus or minus 5 MHz

questions.question: What is an appropriate way to call another station on a repeater if you know the other station's call sign?

choices.A: Say "break, break," then the other station’s call sign, followed by your call sign
choices.B: Say the station's call sign, then identify with your call sign
choices.C: Say "CQ" three times, then the other station's call sign, followed by your call sign
choices.D: Wait for the station to call CQ, then answer with your call sign

questions.answer: Say the station's call sign, then identify with your call sign

questions.question: How should you respond to a station calling CQ?

choices.A: Transmit "CQ" followed by the other station’s call sign
choices.B: Transmit your call sign followed by the other station’s call sign
choices.C: Transmit the other station’s call sign followed by your call sign
choices.D: Transmit a signal report followed by your call sign

questions.answer: Transmit the other station’s call sign followed by your call sign

questions.question: What is an effective way to seek a call from any phone station when not using a repeater?

choices.A: Sign your call sign once, followed by the words “listening for a call;” if there is no answer, change the frequency and repeat
choices.B: Say “QTC,” followed by “this is” and your call sign; if there is no answer, change the frequency and repeat
choices.C: Transmit an unmodulated carrier for approximately 10 seconds, followed by “this is” and your call sign, and pause to listen; repeat as necessary
choices.D: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” and your call sign, then pause to listen; repeat as necessary

questions.answer: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” and your call sign, then pause to listen; repeat as necessary

questions.question: What does the term "repeater offset" mean?

choices.A: The difference between a repeater’s transmit and receive frequencies
choices.B: The repeater has a time delay to prevent interference
choices.C: The approximately half-second delay to allow for the “squelch tail” to be removed
choices.D: The fee charged by the repeater owner or club to provide for maintenance

questions.answer: The difference between a repeater’s transmit and receive frequencies

questions.question: What is the meaning of the procedural signal “CQ”?

choices.A: A shortened form of the term “Contest QSO”
choices.B: “Communication Quality,” used to indicate transmitted audio clarity
choices.C: Only the called station should transmit
choices.D: Calling any station

questions.answer: Calling any station

questions.question: Which of the following is a customary way to indicate a station is listening on a repeater and looking for a contact?

choices.A: “CQ CQ” followed by the repeater’s call sign
choices.B: The station’s call sign followed by the word “listening”
choices.C: The repeater’s call sign followed by the station’s call sign
choices.D: “QSY” followed by your call sign

questions.answer: The station’s call sign followed by the word “listening”

questions.question: What is a band plan, beyond the privileges established by the FCC?

choices.A: A voluntary guideline for using different modes or activities within an amateur band
choices.B: A list of operating schedules
choices.C: A list of available net frequencies
choices.D: A plan devised by a club to indicate frequency band usage

questions.answer: A voluntary guideline for using different modes or activities within an amateur band

questions.question: What term describes an amateur station that is transmitting and receiving on the same frequency?

choices.A: Full duplex
choices.B: Diplex
choices.C: Simplex
choices.D: Multiplex

questions.answer: Simplex

questions.question: What is the purpose of the reverse function on a VHF/UHF transceiver?

choices.A: To reduce power output
choices.B: To increase power output
choices.C: To listen on a repeater’s input frequency
choices.D: To listen on a repeater’s output frequency

questions.answer: To listen on a repeater’s input frequency

questions.question: What term describes the use of a sub-audible tone transmitted along with normal voice audio to open the squelch of a receiver?

choices.A: Carrier squelch
choices.B: Tone burst
choices.C: DTMF
choices.D: CTCSS

questions.answer: CTCSS

questions.question: Which of the following describes a linked repeater network?

choices.A: A network of repeaters in which signals received by one repeater are transmitted by all the repeaters in the network
choices.B: A single repeater with more than one receiver
choices.C: Multiple repeaters with the same control operator
choices.D: A system of repeaters linked by APRS

questions.answer: A network of repeaters in which signals received by one repeater are transmitted by all the repeaters in the network

questions.question: Which of the following could be the reason you are unable to access a repeater whose output you can hear?

choices.A: Improper transceiver offset
choices.B: You are using the wrong CTCSS tone
choices.C: You are using the wrong DCS code
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: All these choices are correct

questions.question: Which of the following would cause your FM transmission audio to drop out on voice peaks?

choices.A: Your repeater offset is inverted
choices.B: Your FM deviation is too low
choices.C: You are talking too loudly
choices.D: Your transmit power is too high

questions.answer: You are talking too loudly

questions.question: What type of signaling to a repeater uses two simultaneous audio tones?

choices.A: DTMF
choices.B: CTCSS
choices.C: GMRS
choices.D: D-STAR

questions.answer: DTMF

questions.question: How can you join a digital repeater’s “talkgroup”?

choices.A: Register with the local Frequency Coordinator
choices.B: Register with the digital repeater control operator
choices.C: Program your radio with the group’s ID or code
choices.D: Program your radio with the DTMF tone used by the talkgroup

questions.answer: Program your radio with the group’s ID or code

questions.question: Which of the following applies when two stations transmitting on the same frequency interfere with each other?

choices.A: The stations should negotiate continued use of the frequency
choices.B: Both stations should choose another frequency to avoid conflict
choices.C: Whichever station was on the frequency first has preemptive rights to the frequency
choices.D: Use subaudible tones so both stations can share the frequency

questions.answer: The stations should negotiate continued use of the frequency

questions.question: Why are simplex channels designated in the VHF/UHF band plans?

choices.A: So stations within range of each other can communicate without tying up a repeater
choices.B: For contest operation
choices.C: For working DX only
choices.D: So stations with simple transmitters can access the repeater without automated offset

questions.answer: So stations within range of each other can communicate without tying up a repeater

questions.question: Which Q signal indicates that you are receiving interference from other stations?

choices.A: QRM
choices.B: QRN
choices.C: QTH
choices.D: QSB

questions.answer: QRM

questions.question: Which Q signal indicates that you are changing frequency?

choices.A: QRU
choices.B: QSY
choices.C: QSL
choices.D: QRZ

questions.answer: QSY

questions.question: What is the digital color code used on DMR repeater systems?

choices.A: An access code which must be programmed into a DMR transmitter to access a specific repeater
choices.B: A code which automatically programs the repeater offset to a frequency chosen by the user
choices.C: A code which identifies the specific CODEC being used so that the repeater can properly decode the audio
choices.D: A code transmitted by the repeater to indicate health and status of the equipment

questions.answer: An access code which must be programmed into a DMR transmitter to access a specific repeater

questions.question: What is the purpose of a squelch function?

choices.A: Reduce a CW transmitter's key clicks
choices.B: Mute the receiver audio when a signal is not present
choices.C: Eliminate parasitic oscillations in an RF amplifier
choices.D: Reduce interference from impulse noise

questions.answer: Mute the receiver audio when a signal is not present

questions.question: Which of the following is a “talkgroup”?

choices.A: A group of amateur radio operators who share email on a specific amateur radio topic
choices.B: An identifier used by DMR to organize radio traffic so that those who want to hear the group aren’t bothered by other radio traffic
choices.C: The members of a net organized for amateur radio operators with a specific common interest
choices.D: A method of automatically alerting all group members to the frequency where any member is transmitting

questions.answer: An identifier used by DMR to organize radio traffic so that those who want to hear the group aren’t bothered by other radio traffic

questions.question: How is squelch adjusted so that a weak FM signal can be heard?

choices.A: Set the squelch threshold so that receiver output audio is on all the time
choices.B: Turn up the audio level until it overcomes the squelch threshold
choices.C: Turn on the anti-squelch function
choices.D: Enable squelch enhancement

questions.answer: Set the squelch threshold so that receiver output audio is on all the time

questions.question: How is a specific group of stations selected on a DMR digital voice transceiver?

choices.A: By retrieving the frequencies from transceiver memory
choices.B: By enabling the group’s CTCSS tone
choices.C: By entering the group’s identification code
choices.D: By inserting a five-pin, pre-programmed code plug

questions.answer: By entering the group’s identification code

questions.question: How is over the air access to Internet Radio Linking Project (IRLP) nodes accomplished?

choices.A: By obtaining a password that is sent via voice to the node
choices.B: By using Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF) signals
choices.C: By entering the proper internet password
choices.D: By using Continuous Tone-Coded Squelch System (CTCSS) tone codes

questions.answer: By using Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF) signals
